land.text: Dos Pilas and its immediate land

predecessors.note: Founded by Tikal; the split event is in the tikal dossier.

capitals.name: Dos Pilas
capitals.note: Approximate site coordinates (the gazetteer has no entry). After 761 the court 'probably' moved to Aguateca, which the page calls a twin capital.

correction.text: Dos Pilas and its immediate land

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). 'In AD 629, the Tikal king K'inich Muwaan Jol II installed his son Balaj Chan K'awiil, aged four, as ruler of Dos Pilas'; drawn as a 25 km radius, the grid's minimum.

correction.text: the Dos Pilas kingdom at its height: 'some 1,500 square miles (3,885 square km)'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'the kingdom covered an area of some 1,500 square miles (3,885 square km)' at its height, which is a radius of about 35 km. The page dates the conquests of Itzan, Arroyo de Piedra and Tamarindito only as 'conquering' in the introduction and Seibal's attack to 735.

region.text: Dos Pilas and its immediate land

ledger.note: 629: Tikal sets up Dos Pilas. 'In AD 629, the Tikal king K'inich Muwaan Jol II installed his son Balaj Chan K'awiil, aged four, as ruler of Dos Pilas', about 110 km southwest of Tikal (Tikal page).

region.text: Dos Pilas and its immediate land

ledger.note: 672: Tikal captures Dos Pilas. 'King Nuun Ujol Chaak of Tikal attacked and captured Dos Pilas in AD 672, driving B'alaj Chan K'awiil into a five-year exile, probably in Calakmul.'

region.text: Dos Pilas and its immediate land

ledger.note: 677: the exile ends. 'This exile was only ended in AD 677, on the same day that Calakmul celebrated a success over Tikal.'

region.text: the Petexbatun lands round Dos Pilas added to the 25 km core

ledger.note: About 679: Dos Pilas grows into a regional kingdom. After 'a humiliating defeat' of Tikal in 679 the page has the kingdom 'conquering Itzan, Arroyo de Piedra and Tamarindito' and covering 3,885 km2 at its height, none of it dated; 679 is a bridging year.

region.text: the Dos Pilas kingdom at its height: 'some 1,500 square miles (3,885 square km)'

ledger.note: 761: Dos Pilas is abandoned. 'In 761 the city was dramatically abandoned after Tamarindito and other Petexbatun centres rebelled'; the royal family 'probably transported itself to the more defensible Aguateca', and the page has the region 'engulfed by warfare in the late 8th century AD' until the last village was 'overrun and itself abandoned in the early years of the 9th century AD'.

wars.name: Tikal-Dos Pilas war

zones.text: Dos Pilas and its immediate land

wars.outcome: Tikal captured Dos Pilas in 672 and held it until 677 ('driving Balaj Chan K'awiil into a five-year exile'); in 679 Tikal 'suffered a humiliating defeat by its smaller rival'.
wars.note: Calakmul had made Dos Pilas a vassal in 648 and the Calakmul page records a counterattack in 677.

wars.name: Petexbatun wars
wars.outcome: In 735 the lord of Dos Pilas attacked Seibal; in 761 Tamarindito and other Petexbatun centres rebelled and Dos Pilas was abandoned. The region was abandoned by the early 9th century.
wars.note: The Maya civilization page dates the storming of Aguateca to 'around 810 AD'.

certainty.note: The kingdom's limits are unrecorded; the 3,885 km2 figure is a page area, not a frontier.

sources.title: Dos Pilas
sources.note: Founding 629, 648 vassal of Calakmul, 672-677 Tikal, 679, kingdom 3,885 km2, 735 Seibal, 761 abandonment.

notes:
NEW STATE. Cliopatria has no Dos Pilas row; the area lies in the 'Mayan City-States' envelope until 849.
COORDINATES. Dos Pilas is not in the gazetteer (listed as a needed place name); the centre -90.27, 16.44 is the researcher's reading of the site, consistent with the Tikal page's '110 kilometers to the southwest'.
END. 761 is the abandonment of the city; Aguateca, the twin capital, held out to the early 9th century (the Maya civilization page has Aguateca stormed 'around 810 AD'), so the state may run to about 810 at Aguateca; the page gives no state-level end date. Cliopatria's envelope drops this area in 850.
VASSALAGE. Dos Pilas as Calakmul's vassal from 648 is in the calakmul dossier; the page does not say whether Dos Pilas returned to Calakmul after 677.
NOT OPENED. Aguateca, Tamarindito, Seibal pages.
